text: The recognition of burnout as an occupational phenomenon. <break time="0.8s" /> By the W H O in 2019. <break time="0.8s" /> Marked an important moment. <break time="0.8s" /> In the discourse on workplace mental health. <break time="0.8s" /> This designation reframes. <break time="0.8s" /> Clinical assessment and organizational responsibility. <break time="0.8s" /> Shifting attention to systemic prevention. <break time="0.8s" /> It invites employers. <break time="0.8s" /> To adopt structural interventions. <break time="0.8s" /> Rather than relying solely on individual level remedies. <break time="0.8s" /> In practice. <break time="0.8s" /> This means clinicians should collaborate. <break time="0.8s" /> With occupational health and leadership. <break time="0.8s" /> To address root causes. <break time="0.8s" /> It signaled a shift. <break time="0.8s" /> Away from viewing burnout. <break time="0.8s" /> As a personal failing or a matter of individual resilience. <break time="0.8s" /> Toward understanding it as a structural issue. <break time="0.8s" /> Rooted in organizational culture, leadership practices. <break time="0.8s" /> And the broader socio economic context of work. <break time="0.8s" /> This reframing is essential. <break time="0.8s" /> As it opens the door to systemic interventions and policy level changes. <break time="0.8s" /> Rather than placing the burden solely on individuals. <break time="0.8s" /> To cope or adapt.
